neighbours.label: the token that opens a given name or quoted phrase after a naming verb or noun ('was called New ...', 'the phrase “...')
fire: The settlers arrived and the place was called New Hampshire.
In 1640 the harbor was named New Amsterdam by the traders.
The journal uses the term “joie de vivre” in that column.
Critics later gave it the title “La Strada” in English.
A small resort nearby is called New Brighton by locals.
The writer borrows the French phrase “déjà vu” at the end.
The region of the first colony was known as New Spain.
They took it from the saying “carpe diem” in Latin.
quiet: The settlers arrived and the place was cold and empty.
In 1640 the harbor was full of ships from the traders.
The journal ran a long piece on French wine in that column.
Critics later praised the film in English.
A small resort nearby is popular with locals.
The writer returns to the French countryside at the end.
The region of the first colony was rich in timber.
They took it from an old book in Latin.

notes: Card flags broad and mostly gate-closed. Probes: ' New' after called or named 0.6-0.8, ' “' after 'phrase' 0.3, but 'called Acme' 0.07 and 'renamed Port Royal' 0.10, so this may be narrower than the label.
